name: Rudy Giuliani
role: Mayor of New York City (1994-2001); US Associate Attorney General; 2008 Republican presidential candidate; lawyer to Donald Trump (2018-2021)
summary: A former prosecutor and New York mayor who ran a tough-on-crime, tax-cutting, pro-market city government while holding socially liberal views on abortion, gay rights and immigration. As a 2008 presidential candidate he stressed a forceful anti-terror and pro-military foreign policy, school vouchers, health savings accounts and free trade; since 2016 he has been a prominent Trump ally.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Called for rebuilding and expanding US military forces and criticised the post-Cold-War 'peace dividend' as 'a serious mistake'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as personally against abortion but pro-choice: 'ultimately a woman should make that [decision] with her conscience and her doctor'; would not criminalize it, though he backs parental consent with bypass and the partial-birth ban.

central-planning.rationale: Praised the defeat of Chavez's referendum: 'the people of his country understand the need for free markets' and Mexicans did not want 'to go toward socialism and communism'.

collective-defense.rationale: Wrote that NATO should dedicate itself to confronting 'territorial aggression' and that 'we will be there for them in times of crisis'.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Describes himself as pro-gay rights, extended all city benefits to same-sex partners in 1998 and in 2015 said he favours gay rights and gay marriage.

decide-locally.rationale: Repeatedly said abortion funding, Roe, campus gun rules and gun regulation should be decided state by state in 'a federal system', though he also backed federal licensing and federal immigration controls.

defeat-communism.rationale: Held up Reagan's handling of Communism as the model for confronting adversaries and said Latin Americans reject the Castro-Chavez path and 'we should stand against it'.

delink-world-market.rationale: Wrote that 'ever more open trade' is essential, that private investment is the best way to promote development, and welcomed China and India's growth as 'new customers'.

democracy-best.rationale: Called democracy 'a noble ideal' and promoting it 'the right long-term goal', but added that elections are 'necessary but not sufficient' and that elected leaders sometimes govern badly.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Wrote that 'elections are necessary but not sufficient to establish genuine democracy' and that democracy needs sound legal and institutional foundations.

democratic-peace.rationale: Wrote that peace is achievable 'to the extent that nations recognize these rights within their own laws' and hoped bringing the Middle East to these ideals would bring peace.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said 'we have to accept the view that scientists have that there is global warming' and that it can be addressed 'in a way that we can also accomplish energy independence', with a project 'similar to putting a man on the moon' for alternatives; no binding emission cuts proposed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Favours open global trade and bilateral and regional deals, and called protectionism 'an agenda for the past'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wrote that the UN 'has proved irrelevant to the resolution of almost every major dispute' and is 'weak, indecisive, and outright corrupt', and that 'we should not expect much more of it'.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Praised NATO and the alliances with Japan and South Korea, said 'we will be there for them in times of crisis', and opposed withdrawal from Iraq.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Listed 'domestic oil, more refineries', 'clean coal' and natural gas among what 'we've got to expand' (Jan 2008).

expand-nuclear.rationale: 'We've got to expand nuclear. We've got to do clean coal'; noted 'we haven't licensed a nuclear power plant in 30 years' while France is 80 percent nuclear (Jan 2008).

flat-income-tax.rationale: Said 'a flatter tax is simply a tax that you can file on one page. As an option, it would be a good idea' (Dec 2007).

force-without-un.rationale: Backed the 2003 Iraq invasion, said the option of acting unilaterally against al-Qaeda in Pakistan should stay open and that military options against Iran stay on the table; wrote that the UN 'has proved irrelevant to the resolution of almost every major dispute'.

free-trade.rationale: Wrote 'ever more open trade throughout the world is essential'; said NAFTA has been good and urged passing the Peru, Colombia, Panama and South Korea deals rather than 'turn our back on free trade'.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Said illegal immigrants could eventually become citizens 'so long as they could read English, write English and speak English' (Jan 2008).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Said on Social Security 'the first thing we have to do is get a consensus behind private accounts if we're going to change it' (Oct 2007).

islam-incompatible.rationale: In 2007 said Islamic terrorists have 'defiled a great religion' and that most Muslims are 'good people', but in September 2026 he reportedly called New York's mayor 'a radical Muslim'; the latest remarks target a person, not Islam as a whole.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A campaign compilation quotes his December 1999 remarks that Israel exists 'to make certain that Jews from all over the world have a place to live', and he called Israel's right to exist a minimum Palestinian recognition requirement.

limit-guns.rationale: Mixed: as mayor he backed written tests and licensing for gun owners, the federal assault-weapons ban and sued gun makers, but as a 2007 candidate said the Second Amendment is an individual right and only 'reasonable' regulation, mostly state by state, is allowed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said at the Oct 2007 debate: 'the free market is our -- one of our greatest assets' and that a president should 'keep taxes low, keep regulations moderate, keep spending under control'.

military-superiority.rationale: Wrote that a realistic peace 'can only be achieved through strength' and called for rebuilding a military able to deter aggression, with ten more Army brigades, more submarines, bombers and missile defence.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mixed: in 2007 he said 'we shouldn't blame an entire group of people', but a September 2026 report quotes him saying the mayor backs a Muslim effort at 'taking over certain parts of America and certain parts of Europe' (partial quote, secondhand).

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Said 'we should empower [parents] by giving them the money, giving them scholarships, giving them vouchers, let them choose a public school, a private school, a parochial school, a charter school, homeschooling' (Dec 2007).

more-religion-public.rationale: Mixed: opposes school prayer but defended a teacher fired for praying with students and said the Ten Commandments are 'part of Western civilization'.

nation-first.rationale: Mixed: wrote that the realist doctrine 'defines America's interests too narrowly' and urged strengthening the international system, while distrusting the UN and stressing American interests.

national-mission.rationale: Said it is 'our moral obligation' to share freedom and ideals with the rest of the world and that extending American ideals must remain the goal of US policy, but 'not by imposing our ideas on others'.

native-born-offices.rationale: Asked at the May 2007 debate whether the Constitution should be changed so naturalized citizens could run for president, answered 'I would say yes'.

open-borders.rationale: Called for stopping illegal immigration 'right at the border' with a physical and virtual fence, more Border Patrol and a tamper-proof ID so no one enters without identifying themselves.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: In June 2007 said 'this is not the time to deal with disruptive issues like this', that in wartime 'you don't make fundamental changes like this' and to rely on commanders' judgment.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Called views that the age of the sovereign state is ending 'naive' and wrote 'there is no realistic alternative to the sovereign state system'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Asked about halting legal immigration (Tancredo's call) said 'I'm very uncomfortable with it' and 'we shouldn't be having a debate about legal immigration'; the problem he addressed was illegal immigration.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wanted regulations kept 'moderate' and blamed economic troubles on what happens 'when we overregulate and we overtax'; said 'less taxation, less regulations'.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Listed 'I drove pornography out of Times Square' among his conservative accomplishments as mayor (Oct 2007).

results-over-ideology.rationale: Gave as the litmus test for immigration legislation what works rather than compromise, asking whether it makes things better, and said 'I believe in [it] from results' when citing his tax cuts.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mixed: urged continuing US help against AIDS and malaria in Africa but wrote that aid not linked to reform 'perpetuates bad policies and poverty' and trade is the most important help.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In June 2015 told Fox News 'I'm in favor of gay rights, I'm in favor of gay marriage. I see it as an issue of equality'; earlier (2007, 2011) he had opposed it. Most recent position counts.

school-vouchers.rationale: 'We should empower parents by giving them the money, giving them scholarships, giving them vouchers' to choose public, private, parochial, charter or home schools; fought for a New York City voucher program.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Said of the Bible 'I don't believe it's necessarily literally true in every single respect', that parts are allegorical or interpretive, and he does not take Jonah in the whale literally.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Wrote that 'private direct investment is the best way to promote economic development', favouring investment and trade over reliance on a country's own resources alone.

separated-powers.rationale: Argued repeatedly that the line-item veto is unconstitutional ('the Supreme Court found that the line-item veto is unconstitutional') against McCain.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Praised NATO and the US alliances with Japan, South Korea and others as vital and wanted NATO membership opened to more states.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Wrote that the next president must 'preserve the gains made by the USA Patriot Act and not unrealistically limit electronic surveillance'; said the president 'must be free to defend the nation' and urged keeping electronic surveillance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said 'we cannot stop doing business with the rest of the world' and that high tariffs turned the depression into a Great Depression; called the Peru, Colombia, Panama and South Korea deals 'good deals for the United States'.

tax-inheritance.rationale: 'We have to get rid of the death tax' (May 2007) and 'eliminate the death tax' at the Dec 2007 Iowa debate.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said 'having higher taxes, in my view, would be very bad for our economy' and urged to 'fight this impulse to raise taxes'; wanted the death tax abolished and the corporate rate cut; no call to tax high incomes more was found.

unions-good.rationale: Mixed within one answer (Oct 2007): 'unions have made a positive contribution' and the UAW pact needed 'a vibrant union', but 'there are ones that aren't good unions' and people 'should have a right to either belong to a union or not'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said 'moving toward socialized medicine would be very bad for our health care system' and that more 'government medicine, socialized medicine, is going to mean a deteriorated state of medicine'; proposed a tax exemption of up to $15,000 to buy private insurance plus health savings accounts instead.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Built New York's workfare system, requiring recipients to take work assignments for benefits; the Pew summary notes he advocates requiring welfare recipients to work or train.

notes: Most answers rest on his 2007-2008 presidential campaign (debates, interviews, a Foreign Affairs essay) because that is when he stated positions across the widest range of issues; later statements override earlier ones where found. Views that changed: same-sex marriage (opposed in 2007 and 2011, supportive by June 2015); his abortion position (pro-choice, with the partial-birth ban, parental consent and the Hyde amendment) is the same in 2007 and 2015. No Giuliani statement on the Dobbs ruling, tariffs, NATO or Ukraine, voter ID, or later gun or immigration policy was found. His post-2020 election claims and Ukraine activities are not tied to any statement in the list. Later pass (2026-11-24): the OnTheIssues compilation pages were used only to find leads; answers now rest on the American Presidency Project transcripts of the 2007-08 Republican debates (s32-s39), his Foreign Affairs essay and the other primary or press sources. Answers whose only support was an OnTheIssues quote that could not be checked in the original (Leadership excerpts, Fox News Sunday, Meet the Press and Kudlow interviews, state-of-the-city addresses) were nulled. Themes searched in the debates: economy, taxes, health care, trade, energy, immigration, guns, abortion, foreign policy, military, civil liberties, education. No Giuliani text was found on campaign finance, central banking, jury trials, torture law, tax havens or most of the newer ideological statements, so they stay null.
